subject: PII scrubbing for request/response logs — qualification and next steps
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@finexa.com>
To: Connor OBrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-09T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up on logging & PII handling from demo

Connor — thanks again for the demo earlier. A couple of items came out of our internal security review that we need to confirm before procurement. Can you confirm the following about Redwood's request/response logging?

- Do you log full request/response payloads by default, or is there an option to only log metadata?
- Is there an out-of-the-box mechanism to redact headers (Authorization, Cookie) and specific JSON fields (user.email, user.ssn)?
- Can trace IDs be retained for observability while redacting PII (we need to link logs to traces without storing sensitive values)?
- What are the retention controls? We need configurable retention per workload; default is 90 days for us.
- For incident forensics, can we export logs (masked) on-demand and does Redwood support storing logs in a customer-managed S3 or GCS bucket?

We'd like a short written response we can share with our security team. Raj (cc'd on future emails) will be the security lead. Planning timeline: procurement in mid-May.

Thanks,
Elena
Product Ops, Finexa Health
From: Connor OBrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@finexa.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-10T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up on logging & PII handling from demo

Hi Elena — great to hear. Short answers below and next steps at the end.

- Default logging: Redwood captures request/response metadata and a configurable request/response body snapshot. By default we store only metadata and a short redaction-friendly snapshot (first ~2KB) unless a customer opts into full payload logging.

- Header & field redaction: Yes. We provide a rules engine that can redact headers and JSON fields at ingestion. Common presets include Authorization, Cookie, user.email, and user_ssn patterns. You can also add custom regex or JSONPath rules.

- Trace IDs: We support preserving trace IDs (X-Trace-ID / traceparent) separately from payload values. Trace IDs are stored as hashed/opaque tokens by default with an option to preserve the raw trace ID for a short TTL (configurable) if your incident process requires it.

- Retention controls: Per-workload retention windows are configurable (1 day — 7 years). Default for hosted customers is 30 days; we can configure 90 days for your workloads and also support an export workflow before deletion.

- Customer-managed bucket: We support streaming masked logs to a customer-managed S3/GCS bucket via TLS and IAM roles. Exports are available as encrypted bundles.

Attachments: I asked our SE to put together a short redaction spec and a sample retention export spreadsheet — see priyom's note below.

Next steps
1) Can you confirm the minimal set of fields you want redacted (e.g., Authorization, user.email, user.ssn)?
2) Would you prefer masked logs routed to your S3 bucket or stored in Redwood with role-based access?
3) Let's schedule a 30-minute technical call next week (priyom will lead). Proposed times: Tue 4/14 10am PT or Wed 4/15 2pm PT.

Thanks — Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@finexa.com>

Cc: Raj Gupta <raj.gupta@finexa.com>
Date: 2026-04-11T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on logging & PII handling from demo

Connor — thanks, that helps. To be explicit:

- Mandatory redactions: Authorization, Cookie, user.email, user.phone, user.ssn, payment.card_number. We expect hashes of identifiers may be kept (non-reversible) for de-dup unless otherwise noted.
- Trace IDs: We want trace IDs available in raw form for 30 days, then hashed after that period.
- Retention: Set workload A (customer-facing API) to 90 days; workload B (batch infer) to 180 days. We also need an on-demand export for forensic pulls that redacts the mandatory fields but includes trace IDs and timestamps.
- Storage: Preference is customer-managed S3 for long-term retention. During the pilot it's okay to keep logs in Redwood for quick access.

Procurement note: we need the SOC 2 report and a short statement that redaction is applied at ingestion (not retroactive), and a short sample of the masked log format. Procurement target: PO issued by 2026-05-15.

Elena

Subject: Re: Follow-up on logging & PII handling from demo — redaction spec + samples attached

Elena / Connor — looping in a short technical follow-up and two attachments (redaction_spec.pdf, sample_log_retention.xlsx). Summary below and what I recommend for the pilot.

Summary / recommended pilot config
- Ingestion: Apply redaction pipeline at the gateway layer. Rules: drop Authorization/Cookie headers; JSONPath redaction for user.email, user.phone, user.ssn, payment.card_number. Where hashes are required, we use salted SHA256 (non-reversible).
- Trace IDs: Preserve raw X-Trace-ID for 30 days; replicate hashed trace token to long-term storage for correlation beyond 30 days.
- Retention: Workload A = 90d (hosted -> replicate masked bundles to your S3 every 24h), Workload B = 180d. We can set lifecycle rules to move older bundles to GCS cold storage if you prefer.
- Exports & forensic pulls: Exports will be generated as encrypted CSV/NDJSON bundles with redaction rules applied. We include timestamps, hashed identifiers (when requested), and raw trace IDs (within the retention window).
- SOC 2 & evidence: SOC 2 Type II available under NDA; we can provide the Report and a short control narrative describing ingestion-time redaction and key management.

Attachments included:
- redaction_spec.pdf (1 page): fields, regex, JSONPath examples, hash-salt policy
- sample_log_retention.xlsx: sample schedule and export filenames for daily/weekly bundles

Next actions
1) Elena: confirm the mandatory redaction list above and whether salted hashing is acceptable.
2) Connor / Finexa: confirm pilot dates (suggest 4/20 start) and whether you prefer S3 export or Redwood-hosted masked logs during pilot.
3) If agreeable, we'll set up a 30-minute tech call (I can do Tue 4/14 10am PT).

Thanks — Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
